found.unsourced_summary: The cluster's design rests on a handful of statements that no member measures or cites. The grid's constraints are taken from hpcworker's own CLAUDE.md, not from the node: the roadmap and the REFORMS checklist both say the login node is CentOS 7 with bash 4.2 and Python 3.6, which is the whole reason the gates split three ways and heavy Python goes to the container, and the VS Code plan admits its shell checks ran under bash 5.2.21. The roadmap states that Wayne State is CephFS with a Panasas home with no source, and the lab recipe only implies it (a CephFS volume, pan_quota). The playbook's cluster generalities (most compute nodes have no internet, home is often read-only, Unix sockets fail on Lustre and NFS, the base matches the RHEL family most clusters run) are stated without sources and the first is contradicted by the lab recipe's site rule. On credentials and sessions: that Anthropic stores Remote Control transcripts appears in the taxonomy spec with no grade and in the VS Code plan sourced only to hpcworker's own notice; that a cloud worker stops at 90 minutes is asserted by the grid review and the Symphony handoff with no measurement, and it sizes the ten-runs-a-day cap; that framework 22 runs several named workers at once is read from code in the several-workers plan while the same day's review says no second worker has ever been started; the seven-day resume in the grid review is the figure the VS Code plan showed to be stale text. On REFORMS: the 32/20/12 split is the checklist author's classification of 2026-10-03, which the roadmap of the same day says was not checked against the paper, and the taxonomy spec carries it as a property of beethoven-research. On the store: both runbooks give the seven-day and six-month refresh-token lifetimes, the review durations (one to three days, several days), the 'store refuses a lower version' rule and 'Google does not verify apps with the write scope' with no citation. On GitHub: the store-upload runbook's Free-or-Team quota and the handoff's Enterprise Cloud are each inferred, not read from a settings page. Smaller unsourced shared claims: a DOI cannot be withdrawn (checklist), the framework empties hpcworker's run folders (connect-the-grid), three refused grid codes lock a student out for fifteen minutes and a grid account takes about two business days (onboarding).
found.stale_summary: Dated states that have moved by 2026-10-22: the roadmap and the REFORMS checklist (2026-10-03) describe hpcworker at framework 11 and the extension at 12.0.0, two repositories, no gates and no beethoven-research; by 2026-10-07 the encapsulation report seals seven repositories and beethoven-research exists, by 2026-10-15 the spec reports splits.py built and Metaflow chosen, and by 2026-10-21 the grid answers framework 22 and Beethoven is 23.x. The roadmap's six owner decisions and the checklist's three open questions are recorded nowhere as answered except decision 3 (the third repository exists) and, in the spec, decision 2 (Metaflow); phase 0's probe, the headless run and the outer loop are not reported built, while phase 5's store release happened on 2026-10-13. The encapsulation report (2026-10-07) still lists the VS Code decision as open and its header still says two pull requests are open; the VS Code plan's status line of 22:33Z that day records the deferral. The VS Code plan is pinned to beethoven-vscode 631226e and hpcworker e77863c, says the live framework version is not established (10, 13, 15, 16 or 17), carries Claude Code 2.1.283 in the image build, dates the relay and ssh timings to 2026-09-28, and lists a dozen behaviours 'not yet measured' (two Remote Control hosts on one sign-in, --continue across a renewal, a claude -p beside remote-control, GPU jobs, the pilot student's end-to-end check); the grid review of 2026-10-21 still lists --continue across job ends and two workers at once as unmeasured. The Chrome runbook (2026-10-13) says 'upload 20.0.0 now', the dashboard images are 9.0.0's, CWS_ON_PUSH stays unset until then and the release.yml pull request is not yet merged; the handoff of the same day lists the 20.0.0 upload, the beethoven-qa v4.0.0 and v5.0.0 tags and beethoven-vscode #11 and #12 as the owner's pending steps; nothing in the cluster records any of them done, and the extension is at 23.x needing another store release. The store-upload runbook (2026-10-08) describes Beethoven as published Private with a testers' group, retired on 2026-10-13, and waits on a PyPI publisher and tag v0.27.0b1. The onboarding (2026-10-13) sends students to the retired testers group, treats the grid's reach to GitHub as unsettled (settled from a compute node on 2026-10-14) and the archive as populated (the next day's guide says the links point at nothing); the connect-the-grid guide says git is untested on the login node while the lab recipe of 2026-09-27 lists git among the login node's allowed commands. The taxonomy spec and manual are 'verified as of 2026-10-15' with beethoven-qa 5.0.0 untagged at v3.0.0 and the extension 20.0.0 pre-release. The playbook's facts were checked against Anthropic's documentation on 2026-10-03 with a 2.1.271 example pin and version-gated features.
